newsitem.title: UK: Firms plan to replace revenue lost by euro - ISMA.
newsitem.headline: Firms plan to replace revenue lost by euro - ISMA.

text.p: European capital market participants are determined to get back the envisaged loss of revenue from some of their intra-European currency-related activites, a study commissioned by ISMA, which involved 900 members across Europe, revealed on Thursday.

The study was carried out with the assumption that European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) would commence on schedule in January 1999. The International Securities Market Association (ISMA) is the international bond market's main self-regulatory organisation.
The third stage of EMU is due to start in 1999, when the euro will be introduced alongside existing European currencies. EMU-participating national currencies would be phased out by 2002.

The study said firms had shifted their attention to strategy in order to generate alternative revenues. At the same time it said they were striving to formulate policies that would maximise their gains from the transition to the euro.
* Gearing of the firm for a changing client base.
* Development of euro-related derivative products - both hybrids and exotics.
* Phasing out of intra-European foreign exchange trading.
* Expansion of non-EMU business, such as emerging markets.
